connections.title: Model providers
connections.subtitle: A model provider = a vendor endpoint and its API key. One provider can drive your agents and Coffer's internal engine.
connections.activeHint: This provider powers Coffer's own model (Settings → Coffer's model).
connections.transcribeHint: Coffer transcribes voice messages on this provider (Settings → Speech to text). Only one provider carries it, and nothing falls back to another.
connections.reachHint: Which agents this provider reaches is set with the reach control — on the provider's row in the list, or on its own page.

errors.baseUrl: Enter a full URL, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1

welcome.title: Bring your own model endpoint
welcome.body: A model provider is a vendor endpoint plus its API key. Add one and every agent Coffer manages can run on it — the key is stored once, in Coffer's credential store.

featureShare.title: One key, every agent
featureShare.body: Store the endpoint and key once; Coffer projects it into each agent's own configuration.

featureCurate.title: Curate the model list
featureCurate.body: Pick which of the endpoint's models are offered, and what kind each one is.

featureEngine.title: Powers Coffer too
featureEngine.body: The same provider can run Coffer's own model for memory organisation.

connections.bulkDeleteConfirm: Delete {{count}} model provider(s)? Their stored credentials are removed too.

detail.modelsHint: Pick which of this endpoint's models this provider offers, and what kind each one is. Every picker downstream is then limited to your picks of the kind it needs — a chat model dropdown never offers an embedding model.
detail.fetchFailed: Could not list this endpoint's models ({{error}}). Your current selection is unchanged.
detail.noModelsYet: This endpoint listed no models. Leave the selection empty and every model it offers stays available.

internalEngine.title: Coffer's model
internalEngine.subtitle: The provider and model Coffer uses for its own passes, such as organising memory.
internalEngine.timeoutHint: How long Coffer waits for one answer from its own model — a memory pass, a knowledge description, one turn of curation, a transcription. A call that runs out of time defers its work and reports success, so set this above what your provider really takes.

transcribe.title: Speech to text
transcribe.subtitle: The provider and model Coffer transcribes voice messages with, before an agent ever sees them.
transcribe.onBody: Voice messages are transcribed on this provider and the agent is handed the text.
transcribe.offBody: Until both a provider and a model are chosen, Coffer transcribes nothing: an agent is handed the audio file as it is, and the recording never leaves this machine. This is a separate provider on purpose — one that serves chat completions often serves no transcription endpoint at all.

upkeep.title: Automatic upkeep
upkeep.subtitle: The passes Coffer runs on its own, without being asked. Each one can be switched off and re-timed.

aggregate.name: Read from agents
aggregate.writes: Reads your agents' own memory files and writes only Coffer's derived tree. No model involved.

distil.name: Distil memory
distil.writes: The model turns the entries read from your agents into Coffer's own notes and rewrites the index. Deleting the tree and re-running reproduces an equivalent set.

curate.name: Derive documents from sources
curate.writes: Coffer's model reads the sources you write and derives the documents your agents read. It never changes a source.
curate.caution: Switch this off and nothing is ever derived: your sources stay as they are, and the documents agents read stay empty.

offline.title: Daemon offline
offline.body: The coffer daemon stopped responding. Capability lists, tool calls, and registrations will fail until it restarts.
offline.notReadyBody: Coffer's background service isn't reachable yet. It usually starts on its own and this notice clears itself once it does; if the problem continues, restart Coffer.
offline.outOfDateBody: This app reused an older background service left running from a previous version. Restart the daemon so the app and daemon run the same version.
offline.reconnectFailed: The daemon restarted, but the app could not reconnect to it: {{message}}. Quit and reopen Coffer.
offline.webRestartHint: The browser can't restart it — run this in your terminal:

welcome.title: One place for everything your agents know
welcome.body: A collection is two folders: the sources you and your agents write, and the topic documents Coffer curates from them. Make one, then let agents read it.

featureEntries.title: What you write
featureEntries.body: You and your agents add source material — notes through Coffer's tools, uploads, Markdown you drop in yourself.

featureDocuments.title: What Coffer derives
featureDocuments.body: Coffer's own model folds those sources into topic documents, and those are what an agent reads.

featureLocal.title: Local-first
featureLocal.body: Everything is plain Markdown on your machine. Nothing is indexed, and no agent reads through a tool of Coffer's.

welcome.title: Nothing distilled yet
welcome.body: Your agents already know things — which service owns what, the trap you hit last month, how this repo is built. They keep that in their own native memories, in their own formats. Coffer reads those and distils them into notes of its own: one file per subject, filed by repository, plus a global partition about you rather than about a project.

featureRead.title: Read, never written
featureRead.body: Coffer only ever reads an agent's own memory. Nothing here is written back into it.

featureShape.title: One subject, one file

featureOneWay.title: It keeps itself current

channels.title: Channels
channels.subtitle: Connect the IM accounts you already use — Telegram and SeaTalk — to your agents.

welcome.title: Talk to your agents from the IM apps you live in
welcome.body: A channel connects one Telegram bot or SeaTalk app to Coffer's chat platform. Pair it with your own account, then message the bot to chat with an agent — replies and notifications all arrive in the IM chat.

featureChat.title: Chat anywhere
featureChat.body: Messages route into an ordinary conversation; the agent's reply comes back to the IM chat.

featurePair.title: Paired to you only
featurePair.body: A single-use pairing code binds the channel to your account; strangers are ignored silently.

featureNotify.title: Push notifications
featureNotify.body: Coffer can push a message to the paired owner — no inbound message required.

dialog.title: Add channel
dialog.subtitle: Secrets are stored in Coffer's credential store; the channel config only carries references.
dialog.name: Name

errors.name: Enter a name
errors.nameFormat: Letters, digits, dash and underscore only
errors.websocketField: Not used with WebSocket delivery — clear it or switch to Webhook

dialog.telegramHint: The token BotFather gave you for the bot.
dialog.seatalkHint: App ID, App secret and Signing secret from the SeaTalk Open Platform app.
dialog.publicBaseUrlHint: Optional. Your tunnel's public address (e.g. https://xxx.trycloudflare.com). Coffer composes the full callback URL from it for you to register on the SeaTalk Open Platform.
dialog.tunnelTokenHint: Optional. With a cloudflared named-tunnel connector token here, Coffer starts and keeps the tunnel running while the channel is enabled (cloudflared must be installed, and the tunnel's Cloudflare ingress must point at http://127.0.0.1:8787).
dialog.machineUnknown: Coffer could not read this machine's id, so the channel has no machine to run on. Try again in a moment.
dialog.deliveryHint: Webhook needs a publicly reachable URL and a signing secret. WebSocket holds one outbound connection to SeaTalk and needs neither. A bot can only use one at a time.
dialog.websocketSdkNote: WebSocket needs SeaTalk's official Python SDK in ~/.coffer/vendor (or $COFFER_SEATALK_SDK_DIR). It is not on PyPI, so Coffer cannot ship it — the channel stays stopped until it is there.
dialog.websocketPortalNote: Switch this bot's event delivery to WebSocket in SeaTalk's Developer Portal too. Its Re-verify only passes while Coffer is holding the connection.

edit.title: Edit channel
edit.subtitle: Change the bound agent or rotate a secret. Leave a secret field blank to keep the current value.
edit.agentHint: New conversations on this channel start on this agent.
edit.rotateHint: Stored in Coffer's credential store; the existing reference is reused.
edit.signingSecretRequired: Webhook delivery verifies every request's signature — enter the signing secret from SeaTalk's Developer Portal.

test.title: Test delivery
test.subtitle: Push a one-off message to the paired peer to confirm delivery works.
test.needsPeer: Pair the channel first — there is no peer to notify yet.

machine.title: Runs on
machine.unboundBody: This channel is bound to no machine, so no daemon starts it and the bot never answers. Pick the machine that should answer it.
machine.unknownBody: This channel is bound to {{id}}, which no machine in the registry claims — it runs nowhere until it is bound to one that does.
machine.handover: Rebinding needs no restart. The machine losing the channel stops within a couple of seconds; the machine gaining it starts after the next sync round brings the change over. Rebinding away from the machine you are on hands over cleanly — binding a channel to this machine while another still holds it can leave both answering until that machine's next round.
machine.notReach: This is which machine runs the adapter. Reach, in the header, is which agents this channel may drive.

pairing.title: Pairing
pairing.instruction: Generate a code, then send it to the bot from your own account. The sender becomes this channel's sole owner — re-pairing replaces the previous one.

callback.title: SeaTalk callback
callback.registerUrl: Callback URL to register on SeaTalk
callback.setBaseUrlHint: Set your tunnel's public base URL in Edit, and the full callback URL to register on SeaTalk will appear here.
callback.hint: Point a tunnel (cloudflared, ngrok) at the local listener address. The reachability test verifies the path and handshake; whether the signing secret matches SeaTalk's is confirmed only on a real event.

websocketState.kicked: Kicked — another process holds this bot's connection

callback.websocketHint: Coffer dials out to SeaTalk, so there is no callback URL, listener or tunnel. One connection per bot: a second Coffer registering the same app kicks this one off. Events pause while the connection is down.

channels.deleteConfirm: Delete channel “{{name}}”? Its adapter stops and the pairing is removed.
channels.bulkDeleteConfirm: Delete {{count}} channels? Their adapters stop and their pairings are removed.

scope.subtitle: Where this is active: which agents can reach it. Out of reach it stays registered, just not exposed or delivered.
scope.machineLocal: Reach is set on this machine only — it is not synced, so each machine you use sets its own.
scope.dormant: No agent selected — dormant. This stays registered but reaches nobody until at least one agent is selected.
scope.inactiveHereAgent: Inactive here — its reach names no agent registered on this machine.

conflict.title: A conflict stopped this round
conflict.body: Two machines changed the same lines of the same document. Nothing was applied and nothing was published — the vault and the pointer are exactly where they were.
conflict.resolve: Resolve them with your own git tools in the working tree below, and the next round carries on from there.

history.description: Every converge round this machine has run, newest first. The rounds that changed nothing are listed too — they are what shows the vault was still converging.
history.empty: No round has run yet. Save a remote, then Converge now to start one.

key.title: Master key
key.hint: Credentials sync as ciphertext only. Another machine can decrypt what this one publishes only once it holds this same key — export it to a file, carry it over a channel you trust, and import it there. It is never written into the repository.
key.fingerprintHint: Matching fingerprints on two machines mean they hold the same key.
key.importConfirmBody: Credentials stored with the current key stay readable only if the new key is the same one.
key.imported: Key imported — this machine now decrypts the credentials it syncs.
key.importedLocked: Key imported, but {{count}} credential reference still cannot be decrypted with it.
key.fileEmpty: That file is empty — pick the key file exported from the other machine.

machines.title: Machines
machines.description: Every installation of Coffer that has converged with this remote. A machine is identified by an id derived from its host, so renaming one costs nothing and reinstalling Coffer does not create a second.
machines.empty: No machines yet — this vault has not converged with a remote.
machines.lastConvergedHint: A day, not a moment: a machine that is running but idle deliberately does not stamp every round.
machines.keyDiffers: Its credentials cannot be decrypted here
machines.keyUnknown: Unknown — one side has published no fingerprint yet
machines.retireBody: Its descriptor is removed from the registry and nothing else is rewritten. Reach is set on each machine and names none, so it is untouched; a channel BOUND to this machine keeps naming it, and runs nowhere until you bind it to another.
machines.derivedNote: This machine's id is stored in a local file rather than derived from the host, so deleting ~/.coffer makes it come back as a new machine and this row has to be retired by hand.

pending.bodyApply: Applying the remote's changes here would remove more documents than the deletion guard allows. Confirm only if you know another machine really did delete this much.
pending.bodyPublish: This machine's own round would publish these deletions to the remote, and every other machine would then apply them.
pending.rebuildTitle: Rebuild this vault from the remote?
pending.rebuildConfirm: This replaces this machine's vault with the remote's and discards anything only this machine has. Use it when this machine's files are genuinely gone. Continue?
pending.reinstallWarning: If this machine was just reinstalled, or restored from a backup, the honest answer is Reject: the documents are missing here, not deleted, and confirming would take the other machines down with it.
pending.titleApply: A round was held: the remote would delete a large part of this vault
pending.titlePublish: A round was held: this vault would delete a large part of the remote

remote.title: Remote
remote.description: One git repository you own. Each round commits what this vault holds, lets git merge it against what the repository holds, and applies the difference back — deletions included. The repository is a rendezvous, not a system of record: delete it and any machine can rebuild it.

errors.url: Enter a git remote URL (https://… or git@…)
errors.interval: Interval must be at least 60 seconds

remote.credentialRefHint: The name of an entry in Coffer's credential store — not the secret itself. The daemon resolves it when it pushes, so the credential never reaches this page, the repository's git config, or any error text.
remote.includeCredentialsHint: Credentials travel as encrypted ciphertext; the master key is never pushed under any setting. A machine holding ciphertext without the key reports those references locked instead of failing quietly.
remote.notConfigured: No remote configured yet. Name a repository above and this vault starts converging with it.

rollback.title: Undo this round?
rollback.description: This puts the vault back to the state it was in immediately before the round that finished {{when}} applied anything. The undo is an ordinary local change: the next round publishes it to the remote, so the other machines follow.
rollback.willUndo: What this round applied here — the undo reverses each of these
rollback.nothingApplied: This round applied nothing to this vault, so undoing it changes nothing here.

join.new: Joined as a new machine — everything the remote held was added, and everything this vault held was kept.
join.returning: Rejoined as a returning machine — its base was recovered from its own descriptor, so nothing deleted while it was away came back.

round.agentResolved: Merged for you by an agent
round.agentResolvedHint: An internal model resolved the conflict on these paths in the working tree. Worth reading if they are your own notes.
round.lockedRefsHint: This vault holds their ciphertext but not the key that opens it. Import the master key from the machine that has it, below.
round.appliedHint: What this round wrote into this vault.
round.publishedHint: What this round wrote into the shared tree.

runs.quietDetail: {{count}} rounds between {{from}} and {{to}}. None of them changed anything, here or on the remote.

sync.subtitle: Converge this vault with a git repository you own, so every machine you work on holds the same knowledge, skills and configuration.
sync.title: Sync

workflow.title: Runs
workflow.subtitle: Deliveries Coffer is carrying: each run advances through the stages its workflow defines, in its own working directory.
workflow.deleteConfirm: Delete "{{title}}"? Its events, attempts, approvals and run directory go with it. The node conversations are ordinary conversations and stay.

empty.title: No runs yet
empty.body: A run is one delivery: you pick a workflow, name what is being delivered, and it advances through that workflow's stages on its own — each task opening its own conversation with an agent, leaving its deliverable behind, and stopping at an approval before anything reaches the outside world.

workflow.notThisMachine: {{machine}} owns this run. Open it there to act on it.

failure.interrupted: Interrupted by a daemon restart — its conversation is intact; retry opens a new attempt.
failure.agent_error: The agent failed during this attempt.
failure.missing_artifact: A required artifact was never written.

feedback.title: Send feedback to this node
feedback.description: Feedback opens a new attempt with what you wrote as its instruction. Say what should be different.
feedback.placeholder: What should this node do differently?

complete.title: Complete this node
complete.description: Marks the node done and hands the run to the next one.
complete.waive: Complete even though a required artifact was never written

adhoc.title: Add an unplanned task
adhoc.description: The task joins this stage as a node, opens with the same shared context as any node the template planned, and leaves its artifacts in the same place.
adhoc.instructionsPlaceholder: What should this task do? You are writing the node's brief.
adhoc.workdirPlaceholder: Leave blank to use the run's own directory

approval.sectionLabel: Approvals this task is waiting on
approval.title: {{tool}} is waiting for approval
approval.expiresAt: Expires {{at}} — after that the held call fails rather than executing.
approval.approveDescription: The held call resumes and reaches the upstream system once. A comment is optional.
approval.rememberRead: Remember {{tool}} as read-only, so it is not held again
approval.rejectDescription: The held call fails with your reason, and the node can act on it. A reason is required.
approval.reasonPlaceholder: Why should this not go through?

nodeConversation.notFound: This task is not part of this run
nodeConversation.subtitle: {{run}} · {{stage}} · {{type}}
nodeConversation.readOnly: This run is advanced by another machine, so this conversation is read-only here.
nodeConversation.notStartedBody: Nothing has run here yet, so there is no transcript. What you write below becomes its brief: the task reads it when the run reaches it.
nodeConversation.byHandTitle: This step is done by hand
nodeConversation.byHandBody: There is no conversation here: a person does this work, not an agent. What you write below joins its instructions.

inputs.dialogDescription: An input is LISTED to every task that opens afterwards, never pasted into it — a collection can be larger than the whole context budget, and a task is an agent with a filesystem.

hints.knowledge: A collection in this vault's knowledge. The tasks are told its name and read it themselves.
hints.file: The file is stored under this run's own directory, so a task can open it from the working directory it runs in.
hints.link: Just the address. Coffer does not fetch it — the task opens it if it can reach it.
hints.repo: A path to a local git repository. Coffer checks it out into this run's own directory on a branch of the run's own, so nothing here can write in your working copy.
hints.note: Something you write yourself, in markdown. Every task is told it is your own words, and you can keep editing it while the run goes.

inputs.removeConfirm: "{{ref}}" stops being listed to the tasks that open afterwards. The collection or link itself is untouched — the run never owned it.
inputs.removeFileConfirm: "{{ref}}" stops being listed to the tasks that open afterwards, and its uploaded bytes go with it.
inputs.removeRepoConfirm: "{{ref}}" stops being listed to the tasks that open afterwards, and the checkout the run was given goes with it. The repository it came from — its branches and its working tree — is untouched.
inputs.descriptionPlaceholder: What this is, in a few words
inputs.noCollections: This vault has no knowledge collections yet.
inputs.removeHint: Stop listing this to the tasks that open afterwards
inputs.removeNoteConfirm: Delete the note “{{ref}}”? Its file goes with it.

artifacts.promoteDescription: Everything this run is made of is copied into a knowledge collection: what its tasks produced, the files you uploaded and the notes you wrote. Links, collections and repositories are not copied — they are somebody else's, already here, or gone with the run — so they are written down as a list of what this delivery read. The run's own directory is left untouched.
artifacts.existingHint: The files are added alongside what is already there; nothing in it is replaced.

create.title: Create a run
create.description: A run freezes a snapshot of the workflow it starts from, so editing that workflow afterwards leaves this run alone. Coffer gives it a working directory of its own, and it starts in draft — mount what it should read on its page, then start its first task.
create.noneEnabled: Every workflow is switched off. Enable one to start a run from it.

templates.title: Workflows
templates.subtitle: The shapes of work this vault knows how to run. A run freezes the workflow it started from, so editing one here leaves every run that is already going alone.
templates.emptyBody: A workflow is the shape of a delivery: the stages it goes through in order, the tasks in each, what each task runs and what it owes. Write one here and every run of it starts from the same shape.
templates.createDescription: It starts as one stage with one task — rename them and add the rest in the editor.
templates.deleteConfirm: Delete "{{name}}"? Runs already created from it froze their own copy and keep going.
templates.descriptionPlaceholder: What this flow delivers, in a sentence.
templates.attemptCeilingHint: How many times this task may be tried before the run stops. There is no unlimited.
templates.tokenBudgetHint: Reaching it pauses the run rather than starting the next task. Leave blank for none.
templates.staleHint: This template names something the vault no longer has. The save will be refused until it is replaced.
templates.instructionsPlaceholder: Added on top of the skill, for what is specific to this flow.
templates.removeEdge: Remove the edge from {{from}} back to {{to}}
templates.addStageDescription: A stage is a step of the delivery. It starts with one task, which you can rename and add to.
templates.editStageDescription: What this stage is called, whether a run may skip it, and where it sends work back to.
templates.optionalHint: A run may skip this stage instead of stopping when it has nothing to do here.
templates.lastStage: A workflow needs at least one stage.
templates.lastNode: A stage needs at least one task. Delete the stage instead.
templates.nodeDescription: One task in {{stage}}: what it runs, what it owes, and what happens when it fails.
templates.sendBackHint: When something here says an earlier stage has to be redone, the run goes back to it and carries on from there. Without one it only ever moves forward.
templates.stagePositionHint: The order is the flow: this stage runs after the ones before it and before the ones after it.
templates.nodePositionHint: Where in this stage the task runs; the stage's tasks run in order.
templates.deleteStageConfirm: Delete “{{name}}”? Its {{count}} task(s) go with it, and so does any route back to it. Runs already created from this workflow froze their own copy and are unaffected.
templates.deleteNodeConfirm: Delete “{{name}}”? Runs already created from this workflow froze their own copy and are unaffected.
templates.editDescription: What this flow is called and what it is for. Its stages and tasks are edited below.
templates.sendsBackToLine: When a task here reports “{{reason}}”, work goes back to {{stage}} — up to {{count}} times.
templates.comesBackHereLine: {{stage}} sends work back here when it reports “{{reason}}”.

context.description: What this run reads and what it has produced, in one place. Mount a collection, a file, a link or a repository at any point in the run's life — every task that opens afterwards is told it is there. Produced files appear as the tasks write them.
context.emptyBody: A run with nothing mounted starts every task from nothing but its workflow. Mount the PRD, the ticket or the repository, and every task opens knowing about it.
context.notText: These bytes are not text, so there is nothing to show here. The file is on disk under the run's own directory.
context.truncated: The head of a longer file — open it on disk to read the rest.
context.resize: Drag to resize the context panel

sendBack.title: Send this back to {{stage}}
sendBack.description: A task describing what you found joins that stage and runs next. Nothing that already passed is reopened — it answered a different question, and it keeps its answer.
sendBack.notePlaceholder: You are writing the brief of the task that will fix it. What did you find, and where?
sendBack.ceiling: This send-back has been used as many times as the workflow allows, so the run failed instead of going round again.

brief.label: Task brief
brief.queuedTitle: What this task has been told

notes.subtitle: Your own words, part of this run's context. Every task is told so.
notes.placeholder: Markdown. Whatever you want this delivery to know that nothing else told it.
notes.pasteHint: Paste a screenshot and it is stored with the run.
notes.emptyBody: This note is empty. Edit it to say what you want every task to know.
notes.notFound: This note is not part of this run
